title: Japanese Army General Staff drafts to Maj.-Gen. Fukushima, 1901: two-digit grid kana table in romanised telegrams (JACAR C09122808300 ff.; catalogue 715)

steps.what: Project JACAR sweep: the five records found and listed as catalogue 715, taking the Latin strings for enciphered romaji; C09122810100 viewed in full.

Contributor: digits and romaji of the five drafts transcribed from the JACAR images (Claude Fable 5.2) before any table was known; the romaji is plain Japanese, garbled in JACAR's record text; all 23 digit runs have even length.
Contributor (#371): the serial table rebuilt from the 1901 incoming telegrams tried on the drafts, with shifts, reversals, complements and other orderings; 21 of 148 pairs fall outside it.

Contributor (#374): '48456 241 mitasigatasi' taken as ノゾミヲ, giving the spacings of the incoming table's o-row; then オオシマノ before 'kotowa' and リコウシヨウ (repeat pattern); 13 values and a grid rule (tens vowel, units consonant) fix the table.
Contributor: all 23 runs decoded; 138 of 148 pairs in the table, 130 counted as read; C09122808400 and C09122812300 in full; five off-grid values (ten occurrences) unread.
Contributor: kana covered by JMdict words of 3+ kana, real table 58 against max 37 of 1,000 permuted grids and max 36 of 1,000 random reassignments; blind Codex transcription 285/296 digits.

Project: decode.py written from the stated rule only; over the first transcription 23 runs, 148 pairs, 136 in the table (138 with the two re-reads the blind reader confirms); every kana string agrees with the contributor's outgoing1901.tsv. The #371 table decoded beside it gives no words.
Project: JACAR images could not be fetched from this session (proxy refused the host); digits not checked against the images.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The table was rebuilt from three words guessed from the clear romaji right after the digit runs in the same drafts, then completed by its grid rule; no translation or outside key was used.
outcome.fraction_read_source: texts/*_reading.md and the contributor's outgoing1901.tsv, digit pairs: 130 of 148 counted as read (10 off-grid pairs and 8 doubtful kana left out); by draft 10/11, 15/15, 48/59, 37/42, 20/21.

validation.notes: Japanese kana plaintext, no Japanese model in lang/; the contributor's JMdict permutation control (58 against max 37 of 1,000) stands in for it.

gaps.detail: outside the grid, apparently word codes; no code list found
first and blind second transcriptions disagree; images not reachable here
digits as on the image per the contributor; slip or misreading cannot be settled without the originals

gaps.item: rest of the 通報綴 after C09122810000

outcome.notes: Catalogue 715. Outside the LLM paper's scope (Japanese; contributed). The digits rest on AI transcriptions only (Claude first, Codex blind second); no human has compared them with the images.

credits.note: Showed the Latin strings are plain romaji, rebuilt the grid table from cribs in the clear romaji, read the five drafts with controls and a blind second transcription (Claude Fable 5.2, Codex, Claude Sonnet; no human check)
Transcription of the five drafts from the JACAR images (data/outgoing1901.txt)

texts.label: February 1901 (undated)
texts.summary: Tamura to Fukushima, Feb 1901: Kamio's (unidentified kekō) is not permitted, and the General Staff means to send him to Himeji.

reading_review.note: Judged as a reader (no Japanese word list): the decoded kana and the clear romaji join into sentences, with holes at word codes outside the table and doubtful kana marked in the reading.

texts.label: 14 February 1901
texts.summary: Tamura to Fukushima, 14 Feb 1901: the matter of Ōshima is under discussion; if he cannot go, how about Kusunose; Shiba will be sent back in any case.

reading_review.note: Judged as a reader (no Japanese word list): the decoded kana and the clear romaji join into sentences, no holes.

texts.label: 2 March 1901
texts.summary: Tamura to Fukushima, 2 Mar 1901, in the aftermath of the Boxer expedition: Li Hongzhang's answer to Japanese advice against a secret agreement, Zhang Zhidong's request that the treaty should not come into being, and a telegram of the same sense from Xi'an; four word codes unread.

reading_review.note: Judged as a reader (no Japanese word list): the decoded kana and the clear romaji join into sentences, with holes at word codes outside the table and doubtful kana marked in the reading.

texts.label: 8 March 1901
texts.summary: Tamura to Fukushima, 8 Mar 1901: the Field Marshal (Waldersee, per the contributor) wishes to come to Japan from Kiaochow Bay; Tokyo is sounding out how he would be received and asks Fukushima to recommend the trip if it looks favourable.

reading_review.note: Judged as a reader (no Japanese word list): the decoded kana and the clear romaji join into sentences, with holes at word codes outside the table and doubtful kana marked in the reading.

texts.label: 1 May 1901
texts.summary: Tamura to Fukushima, 1 May 1901: someone is to return home; the number of relief troops cannot be met until a matter (word code 80) is settled.

reading_review.note: Judged as a reader (no Japanese word list): the decoded kana and the clear romaji join into sentences, no holes.
